subject: Archaeology
title: The Elgin Marbles Debate
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Elgin Marbles Debate.

hook.text: Lord Elgin stripped marble sculptures off the Parthenon in Athens and shipped them to London in 1801.

buildup.text: Britain says Elgin had permission from the Ottoman rulers of Greece. Greece says the Ottomans had no right to grant it.

discovery.text: Greece built the Acropolis Museum with a glass floor overlooking the Parthenon — with empty spaces waiting for the marbles.

twist.text: The British Museum argues that returning them would set a precedent — every museum would have to empty its galleries.

climax.text: The debate is now over 200 years old. Public opinion in Britain has shifted — polls show a majority now supports return.

punchline.text: Greece built a museum with empty shelves. They are still waiting.

quiz.question: What is the British Museum's main argument for keeping the Elgin Marbles?
options: The marbles are too fragile to transport safely
Returning them would set a precedent forcing all museums to return collections
Britain paid a fair price for them at the time of purchase
